title: Navigating the graphical interface of all three systems

videos.script: Ana's phone rings. The designer on the Mac cannot find where downloads go. Ten minutes later the receptionist on Windows has lost the Wi-Fi icon. And the one person who uses the Ubuntu laptop wants to know how to take a screenshot. {{calls}} Three systems, and Ana is looking at none of them. Most support by phone is exactly this: helping somebody find a thing on a screen you cannot see. {{phone}} The good news is that all three desktops are built from the same few ideas. A place to start programs, a strip showing what is running, a corner with the clock, the network and the sound, and windows with buttons to close them. What differs is where each one is, and a handful of habits that trip people up when they move between systems. {{ideas}} In this lesson you will find those parts on Windows 11, on macOS and on Ubuntu's GNOME, use each system's file manager to reach any folder by typing its path, learn the shortcuts worth knowing on all three, and guide somebody through a screen you cannot see. {{steps}} No desktop was recorded for this lesson. The diagrams are drawn from the systems' layouts, and the screens are described. {{honest}}
